item.title: India’s Future Strategic Choices: Complications of Mass
item.description: India is reviving old tools in a new global order, leveraging its history, economic rise, and broadening diplomacy to claim leadership of the Global South while navigating intensifying great-power competition.

item.title: The Weight of History and Alliances in South Africa’s Geopolitical Turbulence
item.description: South Africa’s foreign policy blends liberation-era ties, post-apartheid grievances, and strategic goals. Amid rising U.S. tensions, Pretoria champions multipolarity, sovereignty, and historical justice to shape its global alliances.

item.title: Executive Summary – Fulcrums of Order
item.description: As rising powers reshape the global landscape, the United States must shift from defending the status quo to building pragmatic coalitions, addressing Global South grievances, and engaging hinge states with a clear understanding of their politics.

item.title: Striving for Seriousness: Brazil’s Inclusion and Exclusion from the World Order
item.description: Brazil’s quest for “seriousness” reveals a country shaped by exclusion from the post–World War II order it helped build. Its push for UNSC reform, multilateralism, and regional leadership reflects a deeper struggle for recognition and status.

item.title: Between Two Reefs: Indonesia’s Strategic Culture in the Twenty-First Century
item.description: Indonesia’s long-held doctrine of “free and active” diplomacy has shaped its journey from anticolonial struggle to emerging middle power. This chapter traces what drives Jakarta’s careful navigation between great-power rivalries.

item.title: The United Arab Emirates: From Footnote to Sophisticated Global Partner
item.description: The UAE has evolved from a quiet Gulf country into a hyper-connected power, leveraging capital, and statecraft to hedge globally, disrupt regionally, and reshape ties with the United States, China, Russia, and the Middle East.

item.title: Fulcrums of Order: Rising States and the Struggle for the Future
item.description: As global power diffuses and multilateralism fractures, a set of rising states increasingly claim the mantle of the “Global South,” reshaping institutions, challenging Western dominance, and forcing the United States to rethink how it engages a rapidly changing world.

item.title: Mexico: A Pivotal State on the Global Stage
item.description: Mexico straddles between the Global North and Global South, leveraging deep integration with the United States while guarding its sovereignty. This chapter explores how history, inequality, and geopolitics shape Mexico’s quest for strategic autonomy on the global stage.

item.title: Saudi Arabia’s Strategic Vision
item.description: Saudi Arabia is redefining its place in a multipolar world, shifting from historical insecurity and dependence on great powers to an ambitious strategy of diversification, self-reliance, and leadership across the Middle East and Global South.

item.title: Strategic Ambiguity: Erdoğan’s Turkey in a Multipolar World
item.description: Turkey’s push for strategic autonomy sees it balancing NATO ties, courting Russia and China, and asserting regional influence, showing how Erdoğan’s Turkey both shapes and is shaped by a rising multipolar world.
